findings.reason: The protected Python solution determines the max number of boxes placed into a warehouse accessible from both left and right entrances. It calculates left prefix minima and right suffix minima for room capacities, taking max(left_min, right_min) as the effective capacity of each room. It sorts both box heights and room capacities, matching the smallest fitting box to each sorted room capacity. The solution runs in O(B log B + W log W) time and O(W) space; no candidate is required.

Taking max of prefix minimum (left entrance) and suffix minimum (right entrance) computes the maximum box height that can physically reach room i. Sorting capacities and box heights ensures greedy placement of smallest fitting boxes first.

Directional minima takes O(W) time. Sorting boxes and capacities takes O(B log B + W log W) time. Single pass matching takes O(B + W) time. Auxiliary space is O(W) for the capacity array. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts boxes and warehouse lists, returning the integer count of maximum placed boxes.

The approach accurately details directional prefix/suffix minima computation, effective room capacity derivation, greedy small-to-small sorting and matching, and O(B log B + W log W) time / O(W) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover largest-box two-ended greedy, bipartite matching overhead, repeated box scans, single room warehouses, central bottlenecks, tall rooms behind short entrances, box/room count imbalances, duplicate heights, and zero fitting boxes.
